Palmarosa

Cymbopogon martinii

A grass that smells convincingly of roses.

Sweet, soft and floral despite being a relative of lemongrass. High in geraniol, which is what gives it the rose character, and one of the gentlest oils we carry for skin.

How to use

  • Add 3 drops to a 30 ml bottle of jojoba for a daily face oil.
  • Diffuse 4 drops with geranium and bergamot.
  • Dilute to 1% for a facial mist.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

  • Soft rose
  • Green grass
  • Sweet floral

Who it's for

Daily facial oils

One of the gentlest oils we carry on skin, and widely used in skincare formulation.

Anyone who likes rose but not the price

Shares geraniol with rose, at a fraction of the cost.

Humid weather

Light and fresh in a way the heavier florals are not.

What people get wrong

Assuming it is related to roses. It is a grass, closely related to lemongrass and citronella. The rose character comes from shared chemistry, not shared botany.

Overlooking it because it is inexpensive. Palmarosa is one of the better-value oils in skincare and tends to get passed over in favour of pricier florals that do much the same job.

What it won't do

It is not rose, and in a side-by-side comparison nobody would confuse the two. It is rose-adjacent at a tenth of the price, which is a different proposition.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Palmarosa

Is palmarosa related to rose?

Not at all. It is a grass in the same genus as lemongrass and citronella. The rose-like smell comes from geraniol, a compound it shares with rose oil.

Is it gentle enough for the face?

It is among the milder oils we carry and is widely used in facial formulations, typically at around 1%. Patch-test first, as with anything new.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Around 2% for the body — roughly 12 drops per 30 ml of carrier oil — and 1% for the face. Always patch-test before wider use, and never apply neat.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
